mission_statement: Owner endorses the overall sonic direction; this roster operationalizes it. Specific personnel/reference choices, programs and cue casts remain proposals.
concept: Eight performing core chairs plus a DJ/electronic producer, with specialist guests. Cast a small subset per section; declare physical player/overdub allocation.

director.reference: David Wise and Eveline Fischer / original Donkey Kong Country (1994)
director.responsibility: Theme, emotional role, genre contrast, section arc and ownership of the current musical foreground.

core.function: A warm, singable foreground voice and short answering phrases.
core.habit: Shape a sentence, leave a breath, then answer it. Use register and touch to distinguish the refrain from the verse.
core.uncertainty: If the line meanders, return to the written hook and simplify the answer. Let rhythm guitar carry the chord pulse.
core.tone: Rounded string attack and wood/body, with an articulate melodic center.
core.rest: When pan, flute or keys owns the melody, contribute a brief response or leave space.

core.function: Small chord voicings, offbeat strokes and recognizable rhythmic figures.
core.habit: Interlock with bass and drums. Separate a picked figure from a sustained chord role; keep strokes playable.
core.uncertainty: If the groove feels crowded, choose one rhythmic cell and leave room for the bass response. Use the Ranglin reference for the guitar section's warm melodic/chord relationship.
core.tone: Soft transient, clear chord body, controlled upper-mid bite.
core.rest: Thin to a dyad, single rhythmic note or silence during a featured guitar or keyboard phrase.

core.function: Harmonic movement, voiced accompaniment and occasional melodic leadership.
core.habit: Use clear voice leading and rhythmic replies. Shape a register change or a more open voicing as a section event.
core.uncertainty: If harmony is muddy, choose the important chord tones and a register outside the current lead. If the song needs a new section, let keys take a complete melodic phrase.
core.tone: Warm core with selective bell-like detail and an expressive attack.
core.candidate: Clean piano programs in LoFi Dreams or World Suite require selection/audition.
core.rest: Leave a clear hole when another chord instrument makes its response.

core.function: The low melodic foundation and a memorable rhythmic answer.
core.habit: Write a short identifiable figure that fits the kick and guitar; vary an ending to announce a return.
core.uncertainty: If the groove lacks identity, strengthen the bass figure before adding more percussion. For acoustic-trio passages use John Clayton on the Montreux Alexander recording as the contextual reference.
core.tone: Rounded weight with enough note identity for a small speaker.
core.rest: Sustain or simplify under a busy foreground phrase; a bass-only transition can have its own spotlight.

core.function: Pocket, sectional energy and readable rhythmic punctuation.
core.habit: Develop a groove through accents, small variations and a planned fill at a phrase boundary.
core.uncertainty: If an entrance has no impact, change the kit's register or density. When the producer leads the beat, answer sparsely. For the acoustic-trio context consult Jeff Hamilton on Montreux Alexander.
core.tone: A selected coherent kit with rounded kick, controlled cymbals and believable brush or stick articulation.
core.candidate: Exact BeatBox Anthology kit remains to be chosen for electronic/dance roles.
core.rest: Allow a duo, hand-percussion or producer-led section to carry the pulse.

core.function: Conversation, hand-played movement and acoustic detail within the groove.
core.habit: Use complementary low/open/closed strokes and short answers. Give each percussion instrument a rhythmic purpose.
core.uncertainty: If the rhythm feels generic, study the interaction of the parts and choose a simpler complementary pattern. Udu and other instrument-specific gestures need their own articulation audition.
core.tone: Skin, body and natural decay, with useful dynamics between strokes.
core.rest: A held melodic statement may need only a small response; remove continuous ornament when the groove already reads.

core.function: A lyrical breathing lead, particularly for Sky Lagoon and discovery.
core.habit: Use phrasing, articulation and rhythmic confidence; a complete answer deserves a real breath.
core.uncertainty: If the phrase sounds like a keyboard line, rephrase around breath length and the instrument's useful register. Let another player answer at the phrase end.
core.tone: Breath-shaped onset and rounded center with controlled edge.
core.rest: During another solo, contribute an answering fragment or rest for a full phrase.

core.recording: Coffee Street, The Passage (pan-jazz ensemble reference)
core.function: Opera's principal melodic signature and selected celebratory appearances.
core.habit: State the tune clearly; shape selected held notes with alternating-mallet rolls, accents and natural decay.
core.uncertainty: If a passage is static, vary phrasing or hand the melody to a partner. Check the Greenidge/Provost references for the continuing articulation study; inspect what the actual UVI program supports.
core.tone: A resonant body behind the strike, with clean source headroom.
core.rest: Keep one pan part in Opera; leave other sections and cues to their chosen voices.

core.artist: Multiple reference teams/artists, selected by cue and section
core.recording: KPop Demon Hunters; Madeon; Condard; original DKC context; optional Quantic
core.function: A versatile electronic performing and production voice: pop song architecture, bright dance momentum, chip-based beats, transformed motifs and section transitions.
core.habit: Choose a primary production mode and anchor track for the cue; write a clear hook, groove and planned handoffs. Electronic leads, basses and chords may be original UVI performances; chopped band stems are one option.
core.uncertainty: Select the cue/section reference lane first, then name the part’s job: groove, melody, atmosphere or transition. Keep the job audible and return to the written hook.
core.tone: A warm, full modern mix with selected bright or retro voices. Chip timbres are deliberate instruments, with controlled edge and audible bass identity.
core.candidate: RetroPlug/LSDJ is installed and native hosting verified for Game Boy. Exact BBA/LoFi programs, any UVI Toy Suite installation and NES/SNES-style coverage still need their own verification.
core.rest: An acoustic-led section can give the producer a small texture or no active part; featured electronic sections give the producer a clear phrase to lead.

reference_lanes.reference_artists: KPop Demon Hunters production team: 24, IDO, TEDDY and Ian Eisendrath on the selected songs
reference_lanes.job: Strong instrumental topline, distinct verse/pre-chorus/chorus identities and a purposeful contrasting bridge.
reference_lanes.uncertainty: If the section lacks focus, identify its hook and the instrument delivering it; make the chorus arrival clear through register, harmony and orchestration.

reference_lanes.job: Bright harmonic lift, a buoyant pulse, melodic synth/band exchange and a satisfying return.
reference_lanes.uncertainty: If energy feels flat, change harmonic rhythm, bass movement or sectional texture before simply increasing loudness.

reference_lanes.release: Goes Hard, vol. 4 (Harder not Smarter instrumentals), 2026
reference_lanes.job: Distinctive chip-bass and lead figures, deliberate rhythmic cuts, compact voice economy and sparse breaks.
reference_lanes.uncertainty: If chip parts feel decorative, give one a recognizable bass, rhythmic or melodic job; a glitch must land back on the phrase.

reference_lanes.reference_artists: Condard for Game Boy performance; original Donkey Kong Country composers for SNES scene/form context
reference_lanes.job: Choose a named Game Boy-like, NES-like or SNES-style palette per cue; keep those sound-design targets distinct.
reference_lanes.uncertainty: Specify the intended voice and musical function first. SNES-style sampled color and space do not require turning the entire mix into a chip synth.
reference_lanes.readiness: Owner-authorized RetroPlug/LSDJ installed for authentic Game Boy. This does not establish NES/SNES production-cart or UVI patch readiness.

recordings: Time Is The Enemy, The 5th Exotic (2001)
reference_lanes.job: Optional organic beat/band integration for a cue that actually calls for it.
reference_lanes.uncertainty: Consult only when the cue chooses an organic downtempo context. It is no longer the global producer default.

guests.function: Independent plucked pattern and melodic counterpoint.
guests.rule: Keep the pattern and melody intelligible as a physical plucked performance.
guests.readiness: Native kora state available; focused audition still needed.

guests.recording: Ys, Renaissance of the Celtic Harp (1971)
guests.function: Atmospheric folk color, arpeggiated space and lyrical harp statements.
guests.rule: Use register, decay and deliberate pacing to create an arc.
guests.readiness: World Suite catalogue candidate; select exact program and audition.

guests.recording: Minor Swing with Django Reinhardt, 1937 recording
guests.function: Singing bowed lines, light chamber dance and acoustic jazz responses.
guests.rule: Write bow-length phrases and select supported articulations.
guests.readiness: World Suite catalogue candidate; select exact program and audition.

guests.function: A distinct reed voice for reflective discovery and night colors.
guests.rule: Use a dedicated duduk performance reference rather than transplanting the flute's vocabulary.
guests.readiness: World Suite catalogue candidate; select exact program and audition.

guests.function: A separate player for timbales or auxiliary figures alongside the conga part.
guests.rule: Assign simultaneous parts to a real additional player or a declared studio overdub.
guests.readiness: Selected Latin timbales/percussion programs already rendered in studies.

seating_limit: Options, not simultaneous required tracks. Every section names a lead, a groove leader, supporting roles and resting musicians.
reference_policy: Historical recordings anchor proposed choices. Most chairs have a primary artist plus contextual references; the producer explicitly uses a cue-selected multi-reference matrix. No fresh timed listening analysis or artist participation asserted.
program_policy: UVI soundkits and explicitly requested Sunbird remain the general instrument family. Owner explicitly authorizes RetroPlug/LSDJ as the exception for the authentic Game Boy/chiptune lane; Ember King’s theme is chiptune. New program choices still require audition; no other non-UVI instruments are authorized by this exception.
producer_material: Original performances on licensed UVI instruments, including dedicated electronic lead/bass/chord parts and our own band stems. Preserve dry source, edit and processed part separately. Reference recordings and ROM/sample rips do not become soundtrack material. The owner-authorized RetroPlug/LSDJ lane adds original Game Boy performances and editable song/stem sources; software/ROMs remain private.
runtime_scope: Studio composition and flattened cue delivery; no new runtime DJ or adaptive audio system.
release_scope: Studies/proposals only; demo freeze, human, voice, phone, child and release acceptance remain separate.
